papers.title: Osseointegration of Plasma-Modified Titanium Dental Implants Enhanced by Maca Nano-Suspension in New Zealand Rabbits: An Animal Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives To investigate the potential effect of combined cold atmospheric plasma and Maca extract nano-suspension as a dual implant surface treatment on osseointegration. Materials and methods Maca nano-suspension was formulated and characterized. Thirty titanium implants were placed in the tibiae of ten adult male New Zealand rabbits and were divided into three groups: untreated, cold atmospheric plasma-treated implants, and cold atmospheric plasma + Maca extract-treated implants. Implant stability was assessed using the AnyCheck ® device at the time of placement (primary stability), and then after four weeks (secondary stability). Histomorphometric analysis of the processed bone specimens was performed. Statistical significance level was set at P ≤ 0.05. Results No statistical significance difference was noted regarding the primary stability between the groups, whereas the secondary stability was significantly greater in the cold atmospheric plasma-treated group compared with the untreated control group ( P- value = 0.015). Histomorphometric analysis showed significantly greater percentages of mineralized bone area around implants in the cold atmospheric plasma + Maca group compared with other groups. Conclusion The combination of cold atmospheric plasma and Maca extract resulted in a greater area percentage of newly formed mineralized bone, suggesting a potential beneficial effect on peri-implant bone regeneration.

papers.title: Hybrid Metaheuristic–AI Modeling for Accurate Prediction of CO₂ Solubility in Amine–Ionic Liquid Hybrid Solvents
papers.abstract: Reducing CO₂ emissions from fossil-fuel-based processes requires accurate and reliable predictive tools for designing advanced solvent systems for post-combustion carbon capture. In this study, an extensive experimental database of CO₂ solubility in hybrid amine–ionic liquid (IL) solvents was compiled and modeled using four hybrid metaheuristic–machine-learning frameworks: Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting combined with the Multi-Verse Optimization Algorithm (HistGBoost-MVOA), Tabular Neural Network combined with the Moth-Flame Optimization Algorithm (TabNet-MFOA), Support Vector Regression combined with the Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (SVR-IWOA), and Extreme Learning Machine combined with the Jellyfish Optimization Algorithm (ELM-JFOA). The input variables included temperature, amine concentration, IL concentration, molecular weights of the amine and IL, and CO₂ partial pressure, while the CO₂ mole fraction in the liquid phase (xCO₂) was considered the target variable. To ensure robust model development, outlier detection was performed using the Isolation Forest algorithm, followed by Robust Scaling for data normalization. Model performance was evaluated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation and independent testing based on R², RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and PBIAS, together with Taylor diagrams, centered RMSE (cRMSE), SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap uncertainty quantification. All developed models demonstrated excellent predictive capability (testing R² > 0.96), with SVR-IWOA consistently achieving the highest prediction accuracy and the narrowest uncertainty intervals. SHAP analysis identified the molecular weight of the ionic liquid and temperature as the most influential variables governing CO₂ solubility. The proposed modeling framework provides a robust and interpretable data-driven approach for accurately predicting CO₂ solubility and supports the design and optimization of hybrid amine–ionic liquid solvents for carbon capture applications.

papers.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
papers.abstract: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. In particular, for all three properties, TabPFN applied to Chemprop's own embedding is more accurate than Chemprop's predictions. TabPFN is also among the fastest models we consider, more than an order of magnitude faster than XGBoost. As TabPFN predicts the entire distribution of the target rather than just a single value, it offers built-in uncertainty quantification, which we compare with the empirical distributions of compounds with repeated measurements. Finally, we interpret the predictions using Shapley values, which rank the features by their importance.

papers.title: A first application of split conformal prediction for dose prediction in knowledge-based radiotherapy planning
papers.abstract: Radiation therapy treatment planning is a labour-intensive process prone to inter-expert variability. Deep learning (DL) dose prediction can accelerate this process, but most DL models do not quantify their reliability. In this study, we construct prediction intervals for DL-based radiotherapy dose prediction using split conformal prediction (CP), a model-agnostic and distribution-free method for uncertainty quantification that provides finite-sample coverage guarantees. We propose patient-level nonconformity scores obtained by aggregating voxelwise scores. Specifically, we formulate a maximum aggregation construction, which guarantees simultaneous coverage of the true dose in all voxels of a future patient with at least a user-defined probability, and a quantile-based construction, which guarantees, with the same probability lower bound, that a future patient attains a prescribed minimum level of voxel coverage. We also investigate groupwise calibration for region-specific guarantees and predictive uncertainty scaling for locally adaptive prediction intervals. The methods are evaluated on head-and-neck cases using a deep ensemble model. The proposed constructions achieved empirical coverage consistent with the nominal levels. Maximum aggregation led to conservative prediction intervals, whereas quantile aggregation produced narrower intervals. Groupwise calibration and uncertainty scaling reduced interval widths in some anatomical regions, while providing region-specific guarantees and local adaptivity. This is the first application of split CP to radiotherapy dose prediction. The explicit patient-level coverage guarantees offer a more interpretable characterisation of prediction reliability than raw uncertainty estimates. Split CP could help clinicians assess the reliability of model predictions and identify cases requiring further review.

papers.title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
papers.abstract: Neural Processes (NPs) are flexible meta-learning models capable of uncertainty quantification across diverse applications. However, the standard NP framework assumes access to noise-free inputs. This is unrealistic in many practical settings, where sensor noise or measurement errors are unavoidable. This discrepancy between model assumptions and real-world data can significantly degrade prediction quality and uncertainty estimates. We introduce Denoising Neural Processes (DnNPs), a principled extension of the NP framework that explicitly models input uncertainty. We train DnNPs via variational inference. DnNPs jointly learn to denoise corrupted inputs and perform meta-learning, making them robust to noisy training data. We demonstrate DnNPs' effectiveness on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing consistent improvements in prediction and uncertainty quantification compared to standard NPs. On PM2.5 spatial interpolation from real-world air quality sensors, DnNP reduces RMSE by up to 30% and NLL by up to 73% relative to standard NPs. We also provide theoretical grounding: we show that the Bayes-optimal predictor under noisy inputs belongs to the DnNP model class, and that plug-in models with fixed observation variance incur an irreducible KL divergence gap that DnNP provably avoids.

papers.title: Cost controllability and predictive control of input-constrained monotone systems on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. We establish cost controllability for maximal monotone control systems subject to input constraints, a class encompassing finite- and infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems with colocated input and output. To this end, we employ a recently proposed saturated feedback to derive state-dependent bounds on the closed-loop cost. Our main result is that cost controllability holds globally with semiglobal exponential rate. We first establish this result in continuous time and then extend it to sampled-data systems. Whereas a qualitative detectability-like property is sufficient for asymptotic convergence of the controller, cost controllability requires quantitative rates. We provide two verifiable conditions ensuring cost controllability with explicit exponential rates: coercivity of the sum of system operator and output injection, and exponential detectability of the linear part. Moreover, under the coercivity condition, the resulting MPC scheme without terminal conditions renders the equilibrium globally asymptotically stable with semiglobal exponential rate already for prediction horizon two. We illustrate our results by a nonlinear finite-dimensional system, a semilinear heat equation and a nonlinearly damped wave equation.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
papers.abstract: Start-ups and grade changes remain largely operator-driven, while developing and maintaining dynamic models for model-based control requires substantial engineering effort. Hybrid Offline Learning and Online Optimisation (HOFLON) uses one-step offline reinforcement learning to select actions from historical transition data. In its original implementation, the online objective combines the predicted return from a tree-ensemble critic with an adversarial-autoencoder (AAE) penalty for unfamiliar state-action pairs. We examine the effect of this penalty and replace the critic and AAE with a sparse variational Gaussian-process (sGP) critic. Actions maximise $μ- κσ$, an uncertainty-adjusted estimate of the return from one action followed by the historical operating practice. On the HOFLON polymerisation-reactor benchmark, removing the AAE from HOFLON led to 4 failed start-ups in 15 runs over five critics. At its published weight, the variation in the AAE penalty is four orders of magnitude smaller than the variation in the tree-ensemble critic. Nevertheless, it changes actions when the predicted returns of competing candidates are nearly equal, and paired runs with and without the penalty diverged from the first move. With a Matérn-5/2 sGP critic, $κ= 0$ led to failure in 13 of 15 runs, whereas with $κ= 3$ none of 15 runs (five critics, three noise realisations) failed. The median and lowest returns were 13,464 and 13,398 (HOFLON: 13,393 and 12,411). A squared-exponential sGP critic with learned inducing inputs needed $κ\geq 3$ to remain within the empirical data support in steady state, and then settled with a temperature offset of 2.0 K.

papers.title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV
papers.abstract: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) naturally handles these requirements, but relies on an accurate dynamics model, which is difficult to obtain underwater. In this paper, we present a nonlinear MPCC in all six Degrees of Freedom (DoF) for a holonomic AUV and alleviate the inaccuracies in the dynamics by augmenting the nominal model employed with residual dynamics learned via Gaussian Process (GP) regression. The learned residual is embedded in the optimal control problem through a zero-order robust optimization scheme, which keeps the controller real-time capable at 25 Hz. A simulation ablation shows that residual selection is essential when designing the controller, and simulation and in-water experiments with the Multimodality, Observing, Low-cost, Agile (MOLA) AUV validate the resulting controllers against a nominal MPCC and a field proven Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller.

papers.title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We propose a Koopman model-based reinforcement learning (K-MBRL) algorithm for controlling nonlinear robotic systems with unknown dynamics. The K-MBRL learns a control policy by minimizing an approximate policy objective that combines the analytical immediate cost with an estimate of the future cost evaluated at the one-step predicted state. To this end, we develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based learning method to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics in a linear representation, while a critic function estimates the remaining future cost. This formulation offers two key advantages. First, the linear Koopman dynamics simplify the model-dependent policy gradient computation to a constant matrix product, enabling computationally efficient policy improvement. Second, one-step model propagation mitigates the accumulation of prediction errors associated with long-horizon rollouts while retaining long-term cost information through the critic. The learned policy enables real-time control through feedforward evaluation without online optimization. We establish policy learning convergence guarantees under standard stochastic approximation assumptions. Simulations on HalfCheetah and quadruped four-legged locomotion tasks demonstrate strong sample efficiency and improved performance compared with classical model-free and model-based reinforcement learning baselines. A pendulum swing-up task is used to assess policy gradient approximation accuracy and conduct ablation studies on the learning mechanism and key hyperparameters. The proposed K-MBRL is further validated on a physical quadruped robot performing a challenging sequence of maneuvers: rising to an upright posture supported by two rounded rear feet, maintaining balance during bipedal walking, and safely returning to the ground, as shown in Fig.1.

papers.title: Universal Approximation Theorem for Metaplectic Neural Operators
papers.abstract: We prove universal approximation for metaplectic neural operators on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains. The nonlocal branches are whole-space metaplectic multipliers with zero extension and restriction, associated with any fixed free symplectic matrix. Assuming a smooth, globally Lipschitz, nonpolynomial activation, we obtain compact-uniform approximation of continuous operators from $C^s$ to $C^r$ and from $H^s$ to $H^r$ in the respective output norms, for arbitrary nonnegative integers $s,r$ and finite input and output channel dimensions. In the Sobolev setting, compact input sets must additionally be uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$. One hidden operator layer with one nonlocal branch suffices. A single scalar symbol atom and finitely many positional features are prescribed by the transform and domain independently of the target operator, compact set and accuracy. The proof combines averaging neural operator theory with an exact chirp-conjugated averaging identity and derivative estimates. The result includes Fourier and fixed nondegenerate fractional Fourier multiplier constructions.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
papers.abstract: Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
papers.abstract: Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

The corrections are applied both inside the latent predictor and directly to its predicted latent state, while the pretrained world model remains frozen. We evaluate the approach in simulation and on a real robot under center-of-mass and friction shifts. These changes reduce the success of the frozen model to near zero. Using three interaction episodes for adaptation, our dual-site approach recovers 90\% success under the center-of-mass shift and 100\% under the modified friction on the real robot. Ablations show that correcting both locations outperforms single-site adaptation. Our diagnostics further suggest that much of the learned correction reduces a general prediction mismatch, while successful control also depends on shift-specific information captured during adaptation.

papers.title: Investigating Composite Modeling in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Design
papers.abstract: Scientific design often requires balancing competing objectives that are expensive to evaluate through experiments or simulations. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) addresses this challenge by using probabilistic models to guide the selection of promising designs. In many applications, tunable inputs map to observable intermediate responses, which are then combined through known functions to compute the final objectives. Prior work on Bayesian optimization of composite functions shows that learning from these intermediate responses, which we call Composite modeling, can substantially improve sampling efficiency in single-objective optimization, compared to methods that condition only on black-box observations of the objective function. The benefits of Composite modeling in MOBO, however, remain understudied. In this work, we study the benefits of Composite modeling in MOBO and investigate the factors driving variation in its gains. We first establish single-objective conditions under which intermediate observations provide no additional predictive information beyond objective values, where composite and black box methods use the same warped Gaussian process prior. Controlled numerical experiments with versions of four MOBO methods across eight synthetic and application-inspired scientific-design benchmarks examine how these conditions relate to optimization gains in the multi-objective setting, where the black box approach models the objective functions with a standard multi-output Gaussian process. Both investigations support the claim that composite modeling tends to help more when the function mapping intermediate responses to final objectives is non-bijective and non-affine.

papers.title: GEMOR-GS: Global Extrinsic-calibration-refined Mapping and Online Relocalization for 3D Gaussian-Splatting SLAM
papers.abstract: Photorealistic and metrically consistent world representations are a primary requirement for LiDAR--inertial--visual SLAM systems that serve robots over continuous operation. 3D Gaussian splatting makes such representations attainable by supplying an explicit, renderable, and queryable scene model. We present GEMOR-GS (Global Extrinsic-calibration-refined Mapping and Online Relocalization for 3D Gaussian-Splatting SLAM) to make the Gaussian map geometrically accurate, globally refined, and re-enterable, providing a better appearance for robot perception and decision-making. To improve the 3DGS map, the LiDAR--camera extrinsic is first estimated offline by direct-method alignment over dedicated calibration segments and reused by all following online and offline processes. Under the calibrated geometry, keyframe poses and Gaussian parameters are refined alternately under a gated differentiable-rendering and LiDAR--projection objective. The final global reconstruction is then rebuilt from the refined keyframe schema with all online constraints lifted. For the robot SLAM lifecycle, the method recovers the pose from the 3DGS map after tracking loss through an XFeat bypass map, RANSAC-PnP coarse localization, and Gaussian RGB-D warp refinement. Experiments on one self-collected and five public sequences quantify each element: the offline reconstruction wins all paired keyframes against the online map by 14.3--19.9 dB, improves PSNR by approximately 9 dB over Gaussian-LIC2, and achieves 86--100% held-out relocalization success tied to extrinsic quality. The results show that GEMOR-GS improves the geometric accuracy, appearance fidelity, and re-enterability of the 3DGS map, serving as a dependable robot world model for SLAM and downstream tasks.

papers.title: Multiscale LegONet: Learning Coefficient-Dependent Local Spaces for Composable Multiscale Finite Elements with Localized Error Bounds
papers.abstract: We introduce multiscale LegONet (Ms-LegONet), a plug-and-play learned block for heterogeneous elliptic problems. One network per spatial dimension is trained once on local coefficient patches and reused, without retraining, across coefficient layouts, sources, boundary data and domain sizes within the trained coefficient class. On a fixed primitive patch the network maps the local coefficient to a zero-boundary space, the only learned object. The multiscale basis functions are the harmonic extensions of a fixed set of boundary traces, each a Galerkin solve in that space. Shared interface traces enforce continuity, larger blocks are assembled by recursive static condensation without any parent-scale network, and a localized Céa bound attributes the error of the learned spaces primitive by primitive. The training labels are harmonic responses of single patches, so no global solve enters the training. Against MsFEM, GMsFEM, the neural-operator element method and an end-to-end Fourier neural operator, Ms-LegONet is the most accurate at equal unknowns: its $L^2$ error is $4$ to $150$ times below the baselines on two-dimensional mosaics of $256$ high-contrast primitives, and its median error stays within $0.1$ percentage points of that of exact local spaces in three-dimensional layered media. For each new coefficient it is $1.6$ to $2.3$ times faster than a fine-grid direct solve in two dimensions. In three dimensions it computes the many-query port response of a chain $30$ to $900$ times faster than finite element solves on the same or a finer mesh, at a relative error of $10^{-4}$ against their $6\%$ and $1.6\%$.

papers.title: Evidential Deep Learning with conditional entropy for glaucoma detection
papers.abstract: We propose a novel conditional entropy function as a basis for quantifying predictive uncertainty in Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) for glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images. Using the EyePACS-AIROGS-light-V2 and RIM-ONE-DL datasets for validation, we found that our proposed EDL model regularized by conditional entropy function produced uncertainty estimates with substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and the conventional EDL framework based on Dempster uncertainty. To further probe our models' interpretability, we analyzed Grad-CAM heatmaps using a focus index representing spatial concentration. Compared with the other uncertainty quantification methods, EDL models exhibited greater separation between the index distributions of correctly and incorrectly classified fundus images. In particular, false negatives were associated with localized Grad-CAM activations that were displaced from the optic disc, consistent with its established clinical importance in glaucoma assessment. Overall, our findings suggest that our proposed EDL framework for glaucoma detection provides not only enhanced uncertainty calibration but also admits a more physiologically consistent interpretability.

papers.title: Impact of Reduced-Order Modelling on Sum-of-Squares Region-of-Attraction Certification for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Converters
papers.abstract: With the increasing penetration of power-electronic equipment, the transient stability of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters is increasingly characterized through the region of attraction (ROA) of the post-fault equilibrium. Sum-of-squares (SOS) programming yields certified inner approximations of the ROA, yet its computational cost grows rapidly with system order. Reduced-order models are therefore widely used to reduce computational cost and, more importantly, to enable analytical investigation. However, ROA analyses based on these models often assume that reproducing the converter's transient response, or retaining more dynamics in the correct time-frame, is sufficient to preserve the ROA of the full-order system. Using time-domain ODE simulations as a reference, the SOS-based ROA of each reduced-order GFM and GFL model is assessed against both its own simulated ROA and that of the corresponding full-order model, thereby separating SOS-induced conservativeness from model-order-induced ROA distortion. The results indicate that increasing reduced-order model complexity does not necessarily improve SOS-based ROA fidelity. In the cases examined, more complex reduced-order models yield lower SOS coverage of the full-order reference ROA, despite closer ODE-boundary agreement in some regions. Model selection should therefore consider both full-order ROA fidelity and certified coverage of the practical operating range, rather than model complexity alone.

papers.abstract: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. Across simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, ExRL enables sample-efficient adaptation of a diverse range of long-chunk policies with minimal task-specific hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Fermat ProbCover: Coverage-Based Active Learning on Fermat Distance Graphs
papers.abstract: Active learning aims to reduce annotation cost by selecting the most informative examples for labeling. In the low-budget regime, where uncertainty-based methods often fail, coverage-based active learning methods such as ProbCover have been shown to be effective. However, these methods typically rely on Euclidean distance, which may not adequately capture the underlying geometry of data. In this article, we propose PC-Fermat, a coverage-based active learning method that replaces Euclidean coverage neighborhoods with neighborhoods defined by a Fermat distance, i.e., a data-adaptive distance that reflects the underlying distribution of the data points. To facilitate computation, we construct a weighted Euclidean neighborhood graph and use a truncated shortest-path algorithm to compute the Fermat coverage graph. We also establish sufficient conditions under which this construction exactly preserves the Fermat coverage computed on the complete graph. papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare joint implant loads in high-functioning individuals with hip or knee joint arthroplasties during selected high-impact tasks against a baseline of walking. DESIGN: Exploratory, cross-sectional descriptive laboratory study METHODS: Adults with a total hip arthroplasty (THA, n=11), total knee arthroplasty (TKA, n=4), or unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA, n=3) performed a selected range of low- to high-impact tasks. Musculoskeletal modelling was used to quantify three-dimensional hip (HCF) and knee joint contact forces (KCF). Linear mixed-effects models were used to rank implant loads relative to walking (baseline) and to compare against healthy controls from a prior study. RESULTS: For people with THA, a 45° change of direction generated the highest predicted HCF (8.38 BW, 95% CI 7.70-9.06), followed by running and unilateral hopping. In the small TKA/UKA samples, unilateral hopping and running produced the highest predicted KCF (8.0-9.1 BW). Compared with healthy controls, participants with THA had a lower predicted HCF during walking only (-1.58 BW, 95% CI −2.46 to −0.69). CONCLUSION: Not all high-impact activities produced greater predicted loads than walking. These preliminary data may help inform future efforts to refine activity recommendations, improve regulatory implant testing protocols, and develop computational simulations of implant performance under realistic loading conditions.

papers.abstract: The volumetric energy density (VED) is often used to characterise the process window in laser beam powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M), commonly referred to as laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF). We assessed its explanatory value using an EOS M280 system on two alloys: stainless steel 304L and the TiB2-modified Al–Cu aluminium alloy A20X. The porosity was measured by light optical microscopy. Furthermore, the pore morphology was quantified, and the results were compared with the densities measured using the Archimedes principle. For 304L, the VED explained 71% of the in-sample variance of the logarithmic porosity, compared with 93% for the factorial model. Scan speed dominated, and irregular pores consistent with lack of fusion predominated. For A20X, no monotonic correlation between porosity and VED was detected. A series of tests at constant VED (62.5–64.8 J/mm3) led to an increase in porosity from 0.03% to 1.08%, which was associated with the accompanying increase in line energy; a contribution of the largest hatch distances could not be excluded. At equal scan speed, hatch distances up to 140 µm had no detectable effect, and pores ≥ 20 µm were compact (median aspect ratio 1.15), consistent with keyhole or gas porosity.

papers.title: Hierarchical multi-resonator metamaterial absorber with graphene integration for ultra-broadband solar energy harvesting and machine-learning-assisted performance prediction
papers.abstract: This study presents a hierarchically engineered multi-resonator metamaterial absorber for ultra-broadband solar energy harvesting across the 0.2–3.0 μm spectral range, covering the ultraviolet, visible, near-infrared, and far-infrared regions. The proposed structure integrates a titanium rectangular patch, tungsten square resonator, dual Fe₂O₃ circular inclusions, monolayer graphene sheet, chromium ring resonator, and a SiO₂/Ti substrate stack, all composed of CMOS-compatible, noble-metal-free materials suitable for scalable fabrication. The synergistic interaction of plasmonic and magnetic resonances enables efficient impedance matching and broadband light confinement, resulting in a peak absorptance of 99.94%, an average absorptance of 98.13% over the operating spectrum, an AM1.5 G solar-weighted absorptance of 97.84%, and a 90% absorption bandwidth of 2800 nm. Numerical investigations performed using the finite element method (FEM) in COMSOL Multiphysics were validated through Transfer Matrix Method (TMM), Temporal Coupled-Mode Theory (TCMT), and equivalent LC-resonance modeling, all showing excellent agreement with the simulated results. Comprehensive parametric and power-dissipation analyses reveal that the broadband response originates from cooperative excitation of multiple resonant mechanisms, with the tungsten resonator primarily governing spectral tuning and the chromium ring enhancing bandwidth through surface plasmon polariton coupling. Fabrication tolerance studies confirm robust operation, maintaining average absorptance above 96.9% under realistic dimensional deviations, while polarization-insensitive behavior and angular stability are preserved up to 60° incidence for both TE and TM polarizations. To further accelerate device optimization, a Bayesian Gaussian Process Regression surrogate model was developed for predicting absorptance under geometric and angular variations, achieving mean R² values of 0.9574 and 0.8999, respectively, with RMSE below 0.034. Compared with full-wave FEM simulations, the surrogate model provides an approximate computational speed-up of 3.15 × 10⁵, enabling rapid optimization and uncertainty quantification. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed absorber as a high-performance, fabrication-tolerant platform for solar energy harvesting and thermophotovoltaic applications.

papers.title: Advances in engineered 3D cardiac tissue for functional biosensing, disease modeling, and regenerative medicine
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) engineered cardiac tissues are miniaturized in vitro cardiac models to recapitulate essential aspects of native heart physiology for applications in drug testing, disease modeling and regenerative therapy. Building on advances in microfabrication, biomaterials, bioelectronics and stem cell biology, these systems reproduce myocardial architecture, mechanical dynamics, electrical conductivity, and disease-specific phenotypes. Existing reviews treat biofabrication, biomaterials, functional biosensing, disease modeling, and cardiac regenerative therapy as separate topics, while few have framed these components within a unified micro- and nanoengineering framework that links tissue architecture, functional biosensing, and application-driven performance. This review addresses this gap by highlighting recent advances in biofabrication strategies for precise control over tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments and discusses the incorporation of microelectronic, optical, and mechanical biosensors for real-time, multiparametric monitoring of tissue contractility and electrophysiological activity. We further summarize representative applications in disease modeling such as cardiomyopathies, ischemic injury, and drug-induced cardiotoxicity, as well as the development of bioengineered cardiac constructs and patches as transplantable grafts to restore myocardial function. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward predictive, scalable, and translational cardiac microphysiological systems are discussed.

papers.title: Effects of implant microstructure on drug release of ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) based long-acting implants
papers.abstract: The development of long-acting implants with a core-shell reservoir design is challenging because of their complex structure and prolonged testing requirements. While the polymeric shell has been investigated in a previous study, the present study focuses on the implant core, characterizing its microstructural evolution during in vitro drug release in an aqueous medium using in situ micro-computed tomography. Results revealed progressive water uptake into porous depletion layers that developed during drug release. The mechanisms of water transport and drug diffusion were investigated using depletion layer model films fabricated from the implant core and evaluated using diffusion cells experiments. Permeation of a hydrophilic dye, Allura Red, demonstrated interconnected aqueous transport pathways in the water-filled model films. Separately, drug permeability was directly measured using etonogestrel as the permeant. Etonogestrel permeability in water-filled films was approximately 2.7 times that in dried films, primarily attributed to higher drug diffusivity through the interconnected aqueous pore network. Implant microstructure before and after drug depletion was characterized using high-resolution mosaic field-of-view scanning electron microscopy combined with artificial intelligence-based phase identification, supporting a mechanism in which drug particle dissolution generates pores that subsequently undergo structural evolution. The results support two drug transport pathways: (1) diffusion through the polymer phase and (2) diffusion through an interconnected, water-filled pore network. The effects of pore formation, water infiltration, pore connectivity, and pore shrinkage on drug transport were considered in relation to product development, including raw material properties, manufacturing processes, implant microstructure, and dissolution media. This work provides insights into the drug release mechanisms of EVA-based long-acting implants, material and microstructural attributes influencing diffusion kinetics, and analytical approaches that may support the development of generic Nexplanon ® products.

papers.title: Research Progress on Biodegradable Porous Metallic Bone Implants
papers.abstract: Abstract The clinical efficacy of traditional inert metallic bone implants is limited by stress shielding caused by mechanical mismatch and by the need for a second operation to remove the implant. Biodegradable metals have become a focus of research in bone repair materials because they degrade and are absorbed in vivo, their mechanical properties can be tuned, and their biocompatibility is favorable. The introduction of a porous structure further modulates the apparent elastic modulus of the material to match the host bone tissue and provides a suitable microenvironment for cell adhesion, proliferation, and osseointegration. This review summarizes the characteristics and the current status of research on the three major biodegradable metal groups, namely, the Fe-, Mg-, and Zn-based systems. It compares the advantages and limitations of fabricating porous metallic scaffolds by electrodeposition, sintering, space-holder casting, and additive manufacturing. A mechanistic framework is proposed that links alloy composition, pore architecture, degradation kinetics, and the time-dependent evolution of mechanical properties, in which the weakening caused by matrix dissolution competes with the strengthening caused by the deposition of corrosion and mineralization products. The mechanical compatibility window defined by matching the mechanical degradation rate of the scaffold to the rate of bone regeneration is then analyzed, and a dimensionless ratio of the two rate constants is proposed as a criterion for this matching. Finally, future directions in this field are discussed, with the aim of providing a reference for the development of high-performance biodegradable porous metallic bone implants.

papers.title: No Differences in Patient-reported Outcomes Between the Direct Anterior and Posterolateral Approach for THA: A Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: Background The direct anterior approach (DAA) for THA is seeing wider use because it is purported to deliver a faster postoperative recovery. However, most previous studies comparing the DAA with the posterolateral approach (PLA) were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous patient populations, and the use of outcome measures with ceiling effects. Questions/purposes (1) Does the DAA result in a higher proportion of patients achieving the patient acceptable symptom state (PASS) on the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) after THA compared with the PLA? (2) Are there differences in symptoms, physical function, life activities and participation, health-related quality of life (QoL), or complications between the DAA and PLA in the first postoperative year? Methods A prospective, parallel-group, nonblinded, randomized controlled trial comparing the DAA and PLA for THA was conducted. Patients with primary or secondary osteoarthritis with an indication for THA with an uncemented femoral stem and cemented acetabular component were eligible. Of the 241 patients assessed for eligibility, 53% (128) were included in the study. Fifty-one percent (65 of 128) were randomized to the DAA group, and 49% (63 of 128) were randomized to the PLA group. One patient in each group was lost to follow-up, leaving 98% (64 of 65) and 98% (62 of 63) of patients available for analysis, respectively. There were no between-group differences in baseline or perioperative measurements. The primary outcome was achievement of the PASS on the HOOS at 3 months postoperatively. An a priori sample-size calculation indicated that 60 patients per group were required to detect a 20% difference in PASS achievement between groups (80% power; α = 0.05). With an expected loss to follow-up of 10%, the sample size was set to 65 patients per group. Secondary outcomes included symptoms, physical functioning, participation, and health-related QoL, assessed using patient-reported outcome measures and physical performance tests. Complications were assessed using the Clavien-Dindo classification. Outcomes were assessed preoperatively as well as at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Results At 3 months, the proportion of patients achieving the PASS did not differ between the DAA and PLA for any HOOS subscales, including symptoms (65% [41 of 63] versus 63% [39 of 62], OR 1.03 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.80 to 1.35]; p = 0.80), pain (48% [30 of 63] versus 53% [33 of 62], OR 0.90 [95% CI 0.63 to 1.27]; p = 0.53), activities of daily living (68% [43 of 63] versus 65% [40 of 62], OR 1.06 [95% CI 0.82 to 1.36]; p = 0.66), sports and recreation (55% [34 of 62] versus 58% [36 of 62], OR 0.94 [95% CI 0.69 to 1.29]; p = 0.72), and QoL (73% [46 of 63] versus 71% [44 of 62], OR 1.03 [95% CI 0.83 to 1.28]; p = 0.80). There were no between-group differences in symptoms, physical function, life activities and participation, and health-related QoL at any time point. Complications occurred in 8% (5 of 65) of patients in the DAA group and 2% (1 of 63) of patients in the PLA group (OR 3.05 [95% CI 0.51 to 18.40]; p = 0.21). Conclusion In this randomized controlled trial, the DAA did not improve patient-reported or functional outcomes compared with the PLA during the first postoperative year. In the absence of demonstrated patient-reported or functional benefits of the DAA, surgeons should not represent to patients that the DAA provides advantages in terms of the pace or magnitude of recovery. Future studies powered to detect differences in the risk of complications should be performed to see whether harms are more likely with the DAA than with other surgical approaches. papers.title: Tooth Contact Analysis of Cycloid Mechanism with Segmented Profile Modification Using Numerical Method
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analytical–numerical model for the loaded tooth contact analysis of a cycloidal drive with tooth profile modifications (TPMs). Based on the principles of contact kinetics, elastostatic contact mechanics, and differential geometry, the time-varying normal contact force, contact compression depth, relative sliding velocity, contact friction force, and loaded static transmission error (LSTE) of a cycloidal speed reducer are systematically evaluated. Furthermore, the intrinsic relationship between the transmission accuracy and contact characteristics is elucidated. Numerical parametric evaluations are conducted to identify favorable profile modification parameters by investigating the evolution of contact parameters and LSTE. To effectively reduce the peak normal contact force, a novel segmentation modification model targeting the inflection-point region with strict C1 tangential continuity is proposed along with its analytical mathematical formulation. The validity of the analytical–numerical framework is independently verified against 3D nonlinear finite element contact simulations under multiple load levels. The results indicate that the positive compound modification method is more effective in reducing the maximum normal contact force than single-parameter modifications. A comprehensive comparison reveals that excessive modification significantly increases contact force, backlash, and transmission error due to the shrinkage of active contact areas. A quantitative multi-objective trade-off index is formulated to balance peck force, backlash, and kinematic accuracy. The proposed methodology provides theoretical guidance for improving the tooth surface contact strength, optimizing clearance design, and enhancing the precision of cycloidal transmissions.

papers.title: 3D-Printed OsteoFlux Scaffolds with Radially Graded TPMS Structures
papers.abstract: In native bone, the transition from dense cortical bone to porous cancellous bone reflects a spatial coordination between mechanical support and mass transport. Inspired by this structural heterogeneity, this study proposes an OsteoFlux (OF) scaffold featuring a radially graded TPMS structure together with a corresponding 3D printing strategy. Specifically, a biomimetic TPMS scaffold design integrating a continuous pore-size gradient with an explicit gradient position constraint was developed. Fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations investigating the effects of TPMS topology and gradient parameters on scaffold mechanical and transport performance were performed. The results indicated that the OF scaffold (a Gyroid (G-type) scaffold with an 800-400 μm radial pore-size gradient) achieved the most favorable combination of mechanical stability and fluid transport performance. Finally, an experiment optimizing the BCP slurry system and digital light processing (DLP) printing parameters was conducted. The fabricated OF scaffold exhibited a compressive strength of 3.25 MPa, a compressive modulus of 172.55 MPa, and a permeability of 4.17 × 10-9 m2. In vitro biological evaluation demonstrated favorable cytocompatibility, along with enhanced osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization of mBMSCs under scaffold-conditioned culture conditions. These findings demonstrate that the proposed OF scaffold provides an effective strategy for enhancing the overall performance of porous ceramic scaffolds.

papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Rapid Deformation Prediction in AlSi10Mg Laser Powder Bed Fusion Using Layer-Wise Cross-Sectional Feature Sequences
papers.abstract: Thermal deformation in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) critically affects part quality, yet accurate prediction remains challenging because finite element (FE) simulations are computationally prohibitive. This study proposes a lightweight and interpretable machine learning framework for rapid deformation prediction in AlSi10Mg L-PBF using layer-wise cross-sectional feature sequences. Because L-PBF proceeds layer by layer, ten geometric feature curves extracted from cross-sectional slices along the build direction are treated as time-series sequences, from which 7890 descriptors are generated using tsfresh, an open-source Python 3.9 library for automated time-series feature extraction. Multi-stage feature selection then selects 25 key descriptors, and a Gaussian process regression model with a Matérn kernel is trained using mean and maximum deformation values obtained from inherent strain simulation. On a single held-out internal test set generated by a sample-level 80%/20% split of the development data, the trained model achieved R2 values of 0.89 and 0.85 for mean and maximum deformation, respectively. On the geometry-disjoint independent test set containing three unseen geometries, the model achieved average PCC values of 0.759 and 0.831, RMSE values of 0.0082 mm and 0.0394 mm, and R2 values of 0.521 and 0.532 for mean and maximum deformation, respectively. The corresponding pairwise orientation-order accuracies were 0.753 and 0.812, both higher than the random-ordering baseline of 0.5. These results indicate that the model can capture orientation-dependent deformation trends for preliminary build-orientation screening. Once trained, feature extraction and deformation prediction for a supported part can be completed within seconds, enabling rapid deformation assessment for design and build-orientation screening. Moreover, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)analysis is used to examine model-specific associations between selected layer-wise geometric descriptors and predicted deformation. Overall, the framework provides a rapid and interpretable surrogate for deformation-aware L-PBF design, enabling early-stage build-orientation screening while reducing the need for repeated FE simulations in industrial process planning.

papers.title: Analysis and Mitigation of Phase Imbalance in Sub-Harmonically Excited Brushless Wound-Field Synchronous Machines
papers.abstract: Sub-harmonically excited brushless wound-field synchronous machines (BL-WFSMs) excited by three-phase voltage source inverters inherently suffer from phase current imbalances due to asymmetric electromagnetic armature phase coupling. These imbalances deteriorate torque characteristics, increase losses, and limit the practical deployment of such machines. This paper presents a detailed analysis and mitigation of armature phase imbalance phenomena in sub-harmonically excited BL-WFSMs, focusing primarily on their electromagnetic origin, electromagnetically consistent modeling, and practical suppression techniques. First, conventional sub-harmonically excited BL-WFSM topologies are analyzed, and the root causes of phase asymmetry are investigated using two-dimensional finite element analysis (2-D FEA). The results demonstrate that inherent asymmetries in the magnetic field distribution and phase coupling introduce unequal phase inductance under inverter excitation. Based on these insights, a fractional-slot concentrated winding (FSCW) machine design featuring structurally and magnetically symmetric characteristics is proposed to eliminate the inherent imbalance in the armature phases. The proposed design is then optimized using a Kriging surrogate model and a genetic algorithm to achieve low torque ripple and high average torque in the steady-state operating region. A prototype is manufactured considering the optimized design parameters, and experimental validation is carried out using a three-phase voltage source inverter. The consistency of the 2-D FEM simulations and experimental results confirmed a substantial reduction in phase current imbalance, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed mitigation approach for sub-harmonically excited BL-WFSMs.

papers.title: Comparison of Glycine Air Polishing and a Rotary Titanium Brush for the Removal of a Surrogate Surface Marker from Implants in Class Ib and IIIb Peri-Implant Defects: An In Vitro Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Debridement of the implant surface is the critical point in the treatment of peri-implantitis, and there is no gold-standard instrument available for that purpose. The aim of the present study was to determine whether the difference in efficacy between glycine air polishing and a rotary titanium brush for the removal of a surface marker depends on peri-implant defect type (class Ib vs. class IIIb), to compare the overall efficacy of the two instruments, and to determine whether titanium brush performance varied with repeated usage. Methods: Forty implants (3.8 × 11.5 mm, double acid-etched) were stained with permanent blue ink as a surrogate for contamination and inserted in 3D-printed resin blocks mimicking Monje class Ib and class IIIb peri-implant bone defects, with 5 mm of the implant surface remaining visible. Each group included ten implants according to the defect type and instrument used (brush or air-polishing); within each brush group, five brushes were each used on one implant when new and on a second implant after sterilization. The implants were instrumented for 30 s. Only the frontal aspect of each implant was imaged; standardized photographs taken before and after the procedure were analyzed by image segmentation using hue–saturation–value color space, and the amount of stain removed was analyzed through two-way analysis of variance. Results: Neither main effect reached statistical significance (defect p = 0.063; instrument p = 0.052), but the interaction defect × instrument did (F(1,36) = 7.01, p = 0.012; partial eta squared 0.163, 95% confidence interval 0.009 to 0.379). Air polishing removed more marker in class IIIb defects (56.34%, standard deviation [SD] 19.43) than in class Ib defects (31.05%, SD 16.49; p = 0.016), and more than the brush within class IIIb defects (30.52%, SD 20.71; p = 0.013); none of these pairwise comparisons remained significant under Bonferroni-corrected non-parametric testing. No significant difference was detected for the brush between defect types (p = 1.00) or between first and second use (paired p = 0.364), although the design could detect only large differences. No group achieved complete removal. Conclusions: In this surrogate-marker model, the relative performance of the two instruments depended on defect morphology. The interaction rests on the combination of a higher value for air polishing and a lower, more variable one for the brush in class IIIb defects, and it is not robust to the omission of the three lowest brush values. Ink removal is not equivalent to biofilm decontamination, and a water-based marker may favor the instrument that delivers more fluid; these findings therefore need verification in a biofilm model before they can inform instrument selection.

papers.title: Time Series Analysis in Frequency Domain: A Survey of Open Challenges, Opportunities and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Frequency-domain analysis has emerged as a powerful paradigm for time series analysis, offering unique advantages over traditional time-domain approaches while introducing new theoretical and practical challenges. This survey provides a comprehensive examination of spectral methods from classical Fourier analysis to modern neural operators, systematically summarizing three open challenges in current research: (1) causal structure preservation during spectral transformations, (2) uncertainty quantification in learned frequency representations, and (3) topology-aware analysis for non-Euclidean data structures. Through rigorous reviewing of over 100 studies, we develop a unified taxonomy that bridges conventional spectral techniques with cutting-edge machine learning approaches, while establishing standardized benchmarks for performance evaluation. Our work identifies key knowledge gaps in the field, particularly in geometric deep learning and quantum-enhanced spectral analysis. The survey offers practitioners a systematic framework for method selection and implementation, while charting promising directions for future research in this rapidly evolving domain.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Two-Phase Stefan Problem
papers.abstract: The Stefan problem is a classical free-boundary problem that models phase-change processes and poses computational challenges due to its moving interface and nonlinear temperature-phase coupling. In this work, we develop a physics-informed neural network framework for solving two-phase Stefan problems. The proposed method explicitly tracks the interface motion and enforces the discontinuity in the temperature gradient across the interface while maintaining global consistency of the temperature field. Our approach employs two neural networks: one representing the moving interface and the other for the temperature field. The interface network allows rapid categorization of thermal diffusivity in the spatial domain, which is a crucial step for selecting training points for the temperature network. The temperature network's input is augmented with a modified zero level set function to accurately capture the jump in its normal derivative across the interface. Numerical experiments on two-phase dynamical Stefan problems demonstrate the superior accuracy and effectiveness of our proposed method compared with the ones obtained by other neural network methodologies in the literature. The results indicate that the proposed framework offers a robust and flexible alternative to traditional numerical methods for solving phase-change problems governed by moving boundaries. In addition, the proposed method can capture an unstable interface evolution associated with the Mullins-Sekerka instability.

papers.title: Gradient free aerodynamic design of laminar airfoils and wings using high dimensional Bayesian optimization
papers.abstract: Abstract One major focus of enhancing the fuel efficiency in aviation lies in implementing drag reduction technologies. There exists a significant potential to reduce the viscous drag to facilitate this objective by delaying the laminar to turbulent transition of boundary layers using hybrid laminar flow control. This study evaluates the potential of novel Monte Carlo Bayesian optimization techniques used in conjunction with trust regions for high-dimensional aerodynamic design of transonic laminar airfoils and wings using black-box transition models that lack gradient information. The aerodynamic analysis considered in this study is based on coupled Euler-boundary layer equations with a mid-fidelity conical 2.75D approach, which is more suited for the objective to balance the reduction of viscous and wave drag, in comparison to the conventional low-fidelity panel methods used for fully turbulent designs. A comparative analysis of the underlying acquisition functions governing the Bayesian decision policy is also presented in this work. The Bayesian design framework adapted in this study delivers a 98-dimensional laminar wing with very high aerodynamic efficiency and robust performance within a wide design range. Laminar extensions close to 50% chord lengths are achieved at both upper and lower surfaces of the laminar airfoils and wings when assisted with optimized leading-edge suction distributions, thereby also exhibiting significantly lower viscous drag, while maintaining the wave drag at a practically negligible level, which is a major challenge in laminar aerodynamic designs.

papers.title: Influence of Environmental Knowledge on Attitudes and Behavior of Students Studying Environmental Management
papers.abstract: This study assesses the impact of environmental knowledge on attitudes and behaviors among students studying environmental management versus those in non-environmental disciplines at Nnamdi Azikiwe University. Employing a survey design and Mann-Whitney U test for analysis, it examines whether specialized environmental management education influences students' environmental awareness, attitudes, and behaviour. Findings indicate that environmental management students have significantly higher environmental knowledge, more positive attitudes towards environmental conservation, and engage in more sustainable behaviors compared to their non-environmental peers. These results highlight the essential role of environmental management education in enhancing students' environmental consciousness and commitment to sustainable actions.The study underscores the necessity of integrating environmental principles across academic disciplines to broaden environmental awareness. It suggests active learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and partnerships with environmental organizations as strategies to boost student engagement in environmental stewardship. Additionally, it calls for further research into the long-term impacts of environmental education and its effectiveness across various cultural contexts, emphasizing its importance in preparing future environmental stewards.

papers.title: Semi-automated sex estimation from the cochlea on routine clinical CT: limited incremental value of curvature-based shape descriptors
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Sex estimation is fundamental in forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology, yet classical methods rely on skeletal elements that are often absent or poorly preserved. The bony labyrinth, enclosed within the petrous bone, is a promising alternative owing to its early maturation and taphonomic resistance, and cochlear shape carries a sex-specific signal. However, most approaches depend on manual segmentation, micro-CT, or complex shape-analysis frameworks that limit routine applicability. Objective To evaluate the feasibility of a semi-automated method for sex estimation from cochlear shape using standard clinical CT and automated OTOPLAN segmentation. Materials and methods We analyzed 139 cochleae from 87 adults using clinical CT scans (slice thickness ≤ 0.6 mm). The three-dimensional lateral wall path was extracted with OTOPLAN; after normalization and resampling, curvature- and torsion-based descriptors and scalar cochlear metrics were computed to train a supervised classifier. Preprocessing, feature, and hyperparameter choices were jointly optimized by Bayesian optimization on the training set. Results On an independent holdout set (n = 29), the XGBoost model reached an area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.77 (95% CI 0.55–0.95), with 79% overall and balanced accuracy. Cochlear diameter was the most influential feature, followed by the torsion-to-curvature (τ/κ) ratio across several spiral segments. Conclusion Sex-related cochlear shape information is recoverable from routine clinical CT using a semi-automated pipeline. Although accuracy remains moderate, the approach is non-destructive, scalable, and clinically compatible, offering a potential adjunct for forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology when conventional methods are unavailable.

We developed a 6-week introductory course, aimed at students in the third or fourth year of undergraduate biomedical studies with no or minimal microscopy experience, to help them better understand and utilize these techniques. Through a combination of lecture-based learning and highly interactive hands-on workshops, students are first shown the principles that underlie a particular imaging-based assay and then given the opportunity to perform the assay themselves. In addition to standard assays such as multiwavelength imaging of fluorescent reporter molecules and protein colocalization analyses, lab modules have been designed to allow students to carry out high-end assays such as live and super-resolution imaging using conventional widefield fluorescence microscopes. A final active learning session addresses the analysis, interpretation, and presentation of imaging data. Students then use data they collected themselves to create figures suitable for publication in a research article. According to student feedback, this is appreciated as a highly interactive course that puts theory into practice right away, providing knowledge and skills that can be applied outside of the classroom.

papers.title: Robust depth–yaw control of autonomous underwater vehicles under disturbances and parametric uncertainties
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a simulation-based comparative investigation of four control strategies for depth and yaw regulation of a nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) operating under external disturbances and parametric uncertainties. Proportional–Integral–Derivative (PID) control, Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control (ST-SMC), and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) are implemented within a unified MATLAB/Simulink framework and evaluated under three operating scenarios: nominal conditions, external ocean-current disturbances, and hydrodynamic parameter uncertainties. Controller parameters are held fixed across all scenarios to ensure a consistent comparison. Performance is assessed in terms of trajectory-tracking accuracy, root-mean-square error (RMSE), robustness, control effort, and computational execution time. The results show that ST-SMC provides the most consistent tracking performance among the four controllers. For depth regulation, ST-SMC achieves RMSE values of 0.0920 × 10⁻², 0.9903 × 10⁻², and 0.1819 × 10⁻² m under nominal, disturbed, and uncertain conditions, respectively, with corresponding yaw RMSE values of 0.0250 × 10⁻², 0.3276 × 10⁻², and 0.0270 × 10⁻² rad. These results indicate improved tracking accuracy and robustness relative to PID, FLC, and NMPC across the scenarios considered. Real-time computational performance was profiled at the common 1 ms sampling period used throughout the simulation campaign. PID exhibits the lowest computational cost, with an average execution time of 0.0011 ms per call. ST-SMC also shows very low computational demand, with an average execution time of 0.0142 ms, satisfying the 1 ms deadline in 99.903% of the 100,001 profiled samples. In contrast, FLC and NMPC require substantially higher computational effort, with average execution times of 11.37 ms and 11.0057 ms, respectively, exceeding the 1 ms deadline in all profiled samples; their practical deployment therefore presupposes slower control-update rates or more capable embedded hardware. All four controllers achieved a 100% feasible-solution rate throughout the simulation campaign. Overall, ST-SMC offers the most favorable balance between tracking accuracy, robustness, and computational cost among the investigated strategies, providing a consistent benchmark of the four control approaches within a unified simulation framework. As the reported computational measurements were obtained in a Software-in-the-Loop environment, further Hardware-in-the-Loop and experimental validation on physical AUV platforms is required to confirm real-time performance under operational conditions.

papers.title: Tudo evoluiu, menos a sala de aula: que profissionais de saúde formar em 2026 e como formá-los através das metodologias activas — revisão integrativa
papers.abstract: Introduction: humankind moved from letters to telephones, from spears to remotely piloted war drones, and from messengers to the fastest aircraft. Yet the classroom keeps the layout of a century ago: rows of desks, a teacher who transmits and students who listen. Objective: to analyse the evidence on which health professionals should be trained today and how, focusing on active learning methodologies. Method: six-stage integrative literature review in PubMed, ERIC, LILACS and SciELO (2008–2026), restricted to reviews and complemented by hand searching; selection followed PRISMA 2020. Results: of 708 records, 149 studies were included; 94 of 136 reviews (69%) favoured active methodologies and none favoured lectures. Active methodologies (problem-based learning, team-based learning, flipped classroom, simulation and problematisation) outperform lectures in knowledge, performance and transversal competencies. Lecture-based teaching raises failure risk about 1.5-fold. Main barriers are insufficient teacher training, resistance to change and limited resources. Conclusion: training the 2026 health professional requires changing the classroom itself, placing the student at the centre and the teacher as facilitator.

papers.title: Experimental and Numerical Fatigue Study of TPMS Gyroid Structures Made from Ti6Al4V
papers.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) cellular structures offer high mechanical performance and are increasingly used for load-bearing applications, where fatigue resistance is critical. This study investigates the quasi-static and high-cycle fatigue (HCF) behaviour of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-manufactured Ti6Al4V sheet-based Gyroid structures using experimental testing and numerical modelling. Quasi-static compression tests were performed to characterise the structure’s response, load-carrying capacity and collapse. Compression–compression fatigue tests were conducted under force control into compression to establish the structure’s stress life (S−N) curve. The Gyroid exhibited a repeatable compressive response with a pronounced first peak followed by localisation of deformation within a diagonal collapse band. Recorded cycle counts ranged from approximately 104 to beyond 106 cycles over the investigated stress–amplitude range. A shell-based finite-element model was used to determine local stress fields under the experimental fatigue loads, while fatigue life was estimated using the stress life approach. The numerical predictions showed decent agreement with the experimental fatigue trend, supporting the use of local-stress-based modelling for preliminary HCF assessment of TPMS structures.

Students were assigned to either an experimental (O-E labs) or control (traditional labs) groups. Student performance in the experimental and control conditions was compared using quantitative and qualitative measures. Data sources included lab reports, presentations, surveys, and performance assessments. (3) Results: Students in the experimental group generally demonstrated higher descriptive performance in several laboratory and advanced-concept assessments. However, the inferential analyses did not indicate statistically significant differences between the groups. Qualitative evidence indicated greater reported engagement and collaboration among students in the experimental group through teamwork. They also warrant further investigation using larger samples and designs that permit stronger causal inference. The authors suggest that this approach may represent a scalable model for enhancing remote STEM education. papers.title: Machine Learning Approaches for Demand Forecasting and Intelligent Dispatch in Nigerian Decentralised Energy Systems
papers.abstract: Nigeria’s persistent national grid instability has necessitated a paradigm shift from centralised generation expansion towards predictive and decentralised resilience strategies. This paper presents a PRISMA-inspired systematic review examining the efficacy of machine learning-based demand forecasting and intelligent dispatch for enhancing the reliability of hybrid microgrid systems within the Nigerian context. Through a systematic search across Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, Nature/Scientific Reports, PubMed/PMC, and MDPI, 47 records were identified, with 10 peer-reviewed studies meeting eligibility criteria for narrative synthesis after PRISMA screening. The synthesis reveals that ensemble and hybrid deep learning architectures, particularly Random Forest, XGBoost, and Prophet-LSTM models, consistently outperform single-algorithm baselines, achieving high predictive accuracy with coefficients of determination up to 0.9992 and error reductions of 12-18%. Integration of these forecasting models with mixed-integer linear programming and model predictive control-based energy management systems demonstrates substantial operational benefits, including reduction of grid dependency from 100% to 28.6%, diesel consumption reduction, and carbon emissions reduction of up to 27.5%. The review proposes a context-specific three-layer forecasting-to-dispatch framework comprising data, modelling, and dispatch layers tailored to Nigeria’s data constraints and climatic dynamics. The paper concludes that scalable deployment hinges less on novel algorithmic innovation and more on open data infrastructure, local model recalibration, and integrated forecasting-dispatch implementation in pursuit of Sustainable Development Goal 7.

papers.title: Student engagement in the anatomical sciences: What gets in the way?
papers.abstract: Active learning has become central to anatomical sciences education, yet its effectiveness largely depends on student engagement. Here we define the anatomical sciences as gross anatomy, surface anatomy, neuroanatomy, embryology, histology, and integrated radiology. Educators dedicate substantial effort to implement flipped classrooms, team-based learning, small-group discussions, and other active learning modalities. Despite these efforts, disengagement persists, with students arriving unprepared, participating minimally, and/or perceiving activities as unrelated to assessment. An engagement-centered perspective clarifies these discrepancies and informs more intentional course design. Here, we examine engagement throughout the entire learning cycle, drawing on self-determination theory, cognitive load perspectives, constructivist and social constructivist views, experiential and transformative learning theories, and constructive alignment theory. Common barriers to pre-class engagement include excessive workload, weak alignment with in-class activities, and low perceived relevance. Suggested responses include concise, goal-directed tasks that are clearly linked to learning objectives and incorporate low-stakes accountability and retrieval practice. During class, psychological safety, calibrated challenge, and structured peer interaction are highlighted as central conditions for participation. After class, brief self-testing, spaced follow-up questions, and structured reflection activities consolidate learning. Assessment is positioned as a primary driver of engagement, with an emphasis on constructive alignment to ensure that objectives, active sessions, and summative tasks all rehearse the same kinds of cognitive work. Overall, effective active learning in the anatomical sciences relies less on instructional format and more on fostering learner engagement.

papers.title: Quantitative justification of the advantage of 3d bioprinting over conventional skin transplantation in the reconstruction of burn defects
papers.abstract: Aim: To quantify, using published clinical outcome data, the advantage of 3D-bioprinted and bioengineered autologous skin constructs over conventional autologous skin grafting in the reconstruction of burn defects. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for records published between 1 January 2015 and 28 February 2026;. Three concept blocks were combined with AND, synonyms within each block with OR: (i) skin graft, autograft, donor site; (ii) burn, thermal injury, full-thickness defect, contracture; (iii) bioprinting, bioengineered skin, skin substitute, dermo-epidermal graft. Randomised trials, cohorts, registries and reviews with pooled data were eligible; excluded were case reports under five patients, in-vitro-only endpoints, no extractable outcome, or non-English records. The tissue economy ratio (TER) is the area of defect closed per unit area of donor tissue harvested, cm2/cm2. The iatrogenic donor burden (IDB) is the donor wound area per 100 cm2 closed, IDB = 100/TER; both are computed only from reported values. Quantitative variables are presented as mean (standard deviation [SD]), median (interquartile range [IQR]), or the min-max range across studies, per how the source reported them; qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Results: Forty-six sources were included. Conventional grafting was associated with graft failure in up to 32.3% of patients, post-grafting infection in 41.4%, hypertrophic scarring of the grafted burn area in 8%–67% of patients and of the donor site in 28%-64%, contracture at discharge in 38%-54%, and contracture recurrence in 27.1% of patients at 1 year. In a randomised intra-patient comparison, the tissue economy ratio was 10.76 for a bioengineered autologous dermoepidermal construct versus 1.70 for meshed split-thickness skin grafting, representing a 6.3-fold difference. This corresponded to 9.3 cm² versus 58.8 cm² of donor wound created per 100 cm² of defect closed, respectively, representing an 84.2% relative reduction in donor wound area. Conclusions: The advantage of the bioprinting-based approach is structural and quantifiable rather than marginal and is greatest in patients with the least donor-tissue reserve. Its adoption is limited less by demonstrated efficacy than by challenges related to vascularisation of large constructs, manufacturing lead times, and regulatory classification.
