papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network-Based Inversion of Distributed Temperature Sensing Data for Injection Profile Interpretation
papers.abstract: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS) provides continuous wellbore temperature measurements but does not directly quantify interval water-intake rates. This study develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for water-intake profile inversion in injection wells. A transient coupled wellbore–reservoir model accounts for variable-mass flow, pressure variations, heat transfer, reservoir seepage, and well trajectory. The governing equations, DTS observations, and initial and boundary conditions are incorporated into the loss function to jointly reconstruct the temperature field and identify interval intake rates. Softmax parameterization enforces non-negative intake rates and conservation of the total injection rate. Sensitivity analysis identifies injection temperature, injection rate, and injection duration as the principal factors affecting wellbore temperature. Synthetic cases with different interval thicknesses and permeabilities yield temperature root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 0.1061–0.1268 °C and intake-rate RMSEs of 0.979–1.854 m3/d, with maximum interval relative errors not exceeding 2.611%. A deviated-well case further demonstrates applicability to the tested trajectory variation. For a field injection well, the reconstructed temperature has a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0559 °C and an RMSE of 0.0901 °C. The inferred principal intake intervals and relative allocation agree with reference measurements acquired approximately three weeks apart, supporting the method’s applicability to DTS-based intake-profile interpretation.

papers.title: Life-Cycle Sustainability Assessment of Waste Cooking Oil-Derived Biodiesel: Integrating Environmental, Energy, Economic, and Social Perspectives
papers.abstract: Waste cooking oil (WCO) represents a promising non-food feedstock for biodiesel production, which enables waste valorization while avoiding competition with edible resources. However, existing studies predominantly focus on conversion technologies or individual environmental indicators, and comprehensive sustainability evaluations remain scarce. This study proposes a conceptual LCSA framework and operationalizes it as an assessment matrix for WCO-derived biodiesel, covering the entire value chain from waste oil generation to downstream management. Environmental performance, energy efficiency, techno-economic feasibility, and social sustainability are systematically reviewed, with particular emphasis on how system boundaries, feedstock characteristics, process configurations, and regional conditions affect sustainability outcomes. The research indicates that WCO-derived biodiesel offers environmental advantages over fossil diesel by circumventing agricultural burdens and utilizing waste resources. Nevertheless, the magnitude of greenhouse gas emission reductions varies substantially with transportation requirements, methanol consumption, electricity sources, and allocation approaches. Economic performance hinges largely on feedstock collection efficiency and production scale, while social sustainability remains underexplored due to the lack of standardized indicators. Future work should harmonize life-cycle inventories, enhance uncertainty quantification, integrate techno-economic assessments, and advance large-scale demonstrations to support sustainable deployment within circular economy frameworks.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal variations and control strategies for buckling deformation during laser powder bed fusion thin-walled structures
papers.abstract: Abstract Buckling deformation has been a pervasive challenge in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) of thin-walled structures, severely degrading dimensional fidelity and constraining the fabrication of complex components. Despite its prevalence, the spatial distribution, temporal evolution, and effective mitigation of buckling have remained poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the spatiotemporal characteristics and underlying mechanisms of buckling deformation in LPBF-fabricated thin-walled structures covering a broad range of length-to-thickness ratios, geometries, and build heights. We found that buckling deformation exhibited pronounced periodicity along both circumferential and axial directions. Its evolution proceeded through three distinct stages: thermal shrinkage, initiation of circumferential buckling associated with a concave-to-convex transition (CCT), and subsequent axial propagation. Notably, a hysteretic buckling behavior was identified, which caused false-negative signals in camera-based in-situ monitoring. By combining X-ray diffraction measurements with numerical modeling, we demonstrated that buckling was co-driven by thermally induced compressive stress and critical buckling conditions. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we developed practical control strategies, including auxiliary infrared heating and the introduction of infill lattice structures, which reduced the buckling amplitude from 0.96 mm to 0.045 mm. A buckling sensitivity map integrating process energy density and structural dimensions was further established to guide the design of thin-walled structures. The novel findings advance the fundamental understanding of buckling in LPBF of thin-walled structures, and deliver robust frameworks to mitigate buckling in the manufacture of complex thin-walled structures.

papers.title: Development and Characterization of PLA/PEG/Flax Bio Composites: Influence of Fiber Treatment and Plasticizer Content for Bone-Related Bioengineering Applications
papers.abstract: Biodegradable polymer composites are promising materials for orthopaedic applications because their lower stiffness compared with metallic implants may reduce stress shielding effects. In this study, PLA-based composites containing PEG (0–14 wt%) and flax fiber (5–10 wt%) were fabricated by compression moulding using untreated and pretreated flax fibers, with potential application in orthopaedic fixation plates. The composites were analysed by Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and their tensile, flexural and impact properties were evaluated. The tensile and flexural strength and modulus of composites were improved by approximately 20–30%. SEM results showed that fiber-matrix adhesion was greater than fiber pull-out for the fibers in the fiber-treated samples compared with those containing untreated fibers. Increasing PEG content, the strength and stiffness decreased, and impact toughness increased, particularly for the intermediate-PEG formulations (S3, S4). Similar thermal stability across formulations (TGA) suggested that the effects of treatment and PEG were not influenced on thermal characteristics, but on interfacial and mechanical properties. DSC results indicated that the effects of treatment were surface-limited and not bulk. Thus, the interfacial strength was controlled by fiber treatment, and the stiffness–toughness trade-off was controlled by PEG showing that moderate PEG (S3, S4) treatment was ideal for the mechanical properties of biodegradable orthopaedic fixation.

papers.abstract: This study includes the mechanical and acoustic properties of primitive type (P-type) triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures with five relative densities (RD_35, RD_40, RD_45, RD_50, and RD_55). The mechanical behavior is evaluated experimentally under uniaxial quasi-static compression test to determine the stress-strain response, young’s modulus, plateau stress, critical stress and energy absorption capacity of the structures. The results shows that increasing the relative density significantly enhances the mechanical properties, following a power-law relationship. Furthermore, the acoustic performance of these structures as scatterers of sonic crystals is analysed through numerical simulations and experimental measurements in the frequency range of 3 kHz - 16 kHz, focusing on frequency band gaps and insertion loss. These structures demonstrate significant sound attenuation and shifting of frequency band gap towards lower frequencies as the relative density increases. Additionally, results showed that increasing the number of scatterer rows (up to four) further enhanced insertion loss performance.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Flipped Classroom versus Conventional Teaching Method in Third Professional BAMS Students: A Research Protocol
papers.abstract: Introduction: The “Flipped Classroom (FC)” is an innovative pedagogical approach that enables students to engage with lecture materials outside of class, thereby facilitating more active learning during class sessions. This approach promotes collaboration, deeper engagement with content, skill practice, and meaningful feedback. Creating effective skill-building activities within the FC model is the primary focus of this professional development session. Need of the study: Research contrasting the effectiveness of the FC with conventional teaching techniques is, however, lacking, especially for Kayachikitsa students pursuing a Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS). Despite the growing interest in innovative teaching methods such as the FC, there is a notable lack of research directly comparing its effectiveness with conventional teaching approaches in Ayurvedic education. This gap is particularly evident for Kayachikitsa students pursuing the BAMS. To address this deficiency, the present study has been undertaken to evaluate and contrast the impact of FC pedagogy with traditional teaching techniques in this specific academic context. Aim: To evaluate the effectiveness of FC versus conventional teaching methods in terms of learning outcomes for third-year professional BAMS students in Kayachikitsa. Materials and Methods: This randomised crossover controlled trial will be conducted at Mahatma Gandhi Ayurved College Hospital and Research Centre, Wardha, Maharashtra, India from April 2026 to September 2026 and focus on all third-year BAMS students of the 2021-22 batch. A total of 90 students will be equally divided into two groups, A and B. Group A will be taught Topic I, Grahani, using conventional teaching methods (control group). At the same time, Group B will learn the same topic through the FC method (intervention). Afterwards, a crossover will be done for Topic-II (Pakshaghat). Knowledge will be assessed using multiple-choice pre- and post-tests for both Topic-I and Topic-II. After completing both topics, feedback will be collected via questionnaires for students and teachers. The pre- and post-test results for both groups will be compared using a paired t-test. Intergroup comparisons of the mean change scores between the intervention and control groups will be performed using an unpaired t-test. A significance level is defined as p-value<0.05

papers.title: Analysis of Environmental Factors Influencing Regional Yellowfin Tuna Fishing Using Multi‐Strategy Generalized Additive Model
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Yellowfin tuna ( Thunnus albacares ) distribution is regulated by multidimensional oceanic environmental factors. However, the biophysical mechanisms associated with subsurface ocean parameters remain unclear. Here, we elucidated environmental factors influencing catch per unit effort in the South China Sea and adjacent waters, evaluated hyperparameter optimization for generalized additive models, and provided recommendations for fisheries management. Bayesian optimization outperformed other methods across all metrics, with the lowest AIC, highest fitted‐model pseudo‐ R 2 , and shortest training time. The factors most affecting catch per unit effort were water depth at 12°C, surface height, surface salinity, sea level anomaly, and thermocline upper boundary temperature. Extreme survival depth 450–520 m, surface height 0.4–0.6 m, surface salinity 32.3–32.8 psu, sea level anomaly 0.15–0.22 m, and thermocline upper boundary temperature 28.5°C–30.2°C were suitable. These findings support the development of environmental indicators for dynamic fishing advice and provide insights for ecosystem‐based management of yellowfin tuna fisheries.

papers.title: A Unified Interactive Python Platform for Teaching Wave Optics: From Fraunhofer Diffraction to Resolution Limits
papers.abstract: Abstract Diffraction is a fundamental phenomenon in wave optics, yet its abstract mathematical formulation-particularly the transition from single-slit diffraction to circular aperture diffraction and Babinet's principle-often poses significant conceptual challenges for undergraduate students. Traditional lecture-based instruction, relying heavily on analytical derivations and static diagrams, frequently fails to provide students with an intuitive grasp of how aperture geometry determines diffraction patterns and how the Rayleigh criterion sets the fundamental limit of optical resolution. To address these challenges, we develop an integrated Python-based interactive teaching toolkit comprising three complementary simulation modules: a multi-shape diffraction simulator supporting single-slit, circular, square, and rectangular apertures; a filament diameter measurement tool based on Babinet's principle with built-in uncertainty propagation; and a Rayleigh criterion explorer that visualizes the continuous transition from unresolved to resolved two-point images. Built with PyQt5 and Matplotlib, and underpinned by NumPy and SciPy, the toolkit allows students to adjust key physical parameters-wavelength, aperture size, screen distance, and object separation-in real time and observe corresponding changes in diffraction patterns, intensity profiles, and resolution status. A real-time Fresnel-number diagnostic alerts users when the far-field approximation becomes invalid, fostering critical reflection on the domain of applicability of theoretical models. The simulations render abstract concepts such as Fraunhofer diffraction, Airy disk formation, Babinet's principle, and the Rayleigh criterion more tangible, while also promoting active learning and quantitative experimental reasoning. We present this toolkit as a low-cost, platform-independent resource for integrating computational physics into the undergraduate optics curriculum.

papers.title: A Self-Driving Laboratory for Accelerated Electrolyte Discovery
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of electrochemical materials is constrained by extensive formulation spaces and the low throughput of manual screening. Here, we report a self-driving electrochemical laboratory integrating liquid-handling robotics, online electroanalysis, and Bayesian optimization to accelerate electrolyte discovery. Operating in a 96-well microtiter format, the platform automatically formulates candidate electrolytes, performs temperature-controlled electrochemical measurements, and iteratively updates surrogate models to explore high-dimensional chemical spaces. This framework was applied to the development of high-entropy aqueous electrolytes for low-temperature zinc metal batteries. The system screened hundreds of formulations, and multiobjective optimization yielded an electrolyte with a conductivity of 134.1 mS cm–1 and an electrochemical stability window of 2.50 V, with ∼2019 h of cycling stability in symmetric cells at –20 °C. This approach significantly reduces experimental labor while accelerating the development of electrochemical materials.

papers.title: Nitrosyl coordination compounds: a comprehensive review of synthetic strategies, bonding elucidation, spectroscopic diagnostics, and computational intelligence from DFT to machine learning and generative AI
papers.abstract: Abstract Nitrosyl coordination compounds have undergone a remarkable evolution from Priestley’s serendipitous discovery of nitric oxide to their current standing as versatile molecular platforms at the forefront of modern coordination chemistry, bioinorganic signaling, catalysis, and materials science. This comprehensive review presents an integrated and forward-looking examination of metal–nitrosyl chemistry that systematically bridges classical synthetic methodologies, fundamental bonding paradigms, advanced spectroscopic diagnostics, and cutting-edge computational intelligence. The synthetic landscape is critically surveyed as a decision-oriented framework encompassing direct NO gas reactions, nitrosonium salts, hydroxylamine-mediated protocols, nitrite-based routes, coordinated NO transfer strategies, and emerging green chemistry approaches, with particular emphasis on method selection criteria based on metal identity, ligand sensitivity, scalability, and sustainability imperatives. The bonding narrative is rigorously dissected through the classical lenses of valence-bond theory and molecular orbital analysis, culminating in the modern DFT-based understanding that has revolutionized our comprehension of the elusive M−NO interaction; the linear–bent dichotomy, elegantly captured by the Enemark–Feltham formalism, is established as a predictive tool for rationalizing electron counting, donor capacity, and reactivity patterns, while the non-innocent behaviour of NO-manifesting as valence tautomerism, electron-sink functionality, and dynamic geometric isomerism, is underscored as a fundamental property underpinning catalytic and signalling functions. Spectroscopic characterisation is presented as an integrated diagnostic toolkit wherein complementary techniques, including IR and Raman vibrational spectroscopy, UV–Vis–NIR electronic spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), 15 N nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and Mössbauer spectroscopy, collectively resolve structural, electronic, and magnetic ambiguities through a logically tiered workflow. A distinctive and transformative feature of this review is the extensive coverage of computational intelligence paradigms that have reshaped nitrosyl chemistry: density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) for accurate geometry optimization, vibrational prediction, spectral simulation, and mechanistic elucidation; machine learning algorithms including random forests, support vector machines, XGBoost, and Gaussian processes for rapid high-throughput property prediction of ν (NO) frequencies, M−N bond lengths, M–N–O bond angles, and magnetic properties; generative artificial intelligence through variational autoencoders and generative adversarial networks for de novo molecular design with targeted property constraints; physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for inverse problem-solving and kinetic modelling; and Bayesian uncertainty quantification for robust decision-making through aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty assessment. This work establishes nitrosyl chemistry as a vibrant, interdisciplinary frontier where molecular innovation converges with computational intelligence, and it serves as an authoritative, decision-oriented reference for both newcomers and experienced practitioners across inorganic chemistry, catalysis, bioinorganic chemistry, and materials science.

papers.title: Transmission patterns and future forecasting of mpox: a review of mathematical modelling approaches for prediction and public health preparedness
papers.abstract: Mpox has shifted from a disease mainly associated with zoonotic spillover in Central and West Africa to a recurrent global public-health threat involving sexual-contact networks, household transmission, international mobility, ecological persistence and clade-specific uncertainty. Mathematical models have clarified important mechanisms in the 2022 clade IIb outbreak, including the role of heavy-tailed sexual-contact distributions, behavioural adaptation, vaccination and case isolation. However, the literature remains less mature in one respect that is essential for preparedness: the conversion of transmission insight into reliable, setting-specific forecasts. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed modelling evidence on mpox transmission patterns and evaluates the extent to which existing compartmental, stochastic, network, agent-based, phylodynamic and time-series models support future outbreak prediction. The review identifies four recurring gaps: insufficient prospective validation, weak integration of spatial and cross-regional lags, limited clade-specific parameterization for clade I/Ib risk, and inadequate incorporation of immunity, reporting delay and surveillance uncertainty. We propose a forecasting-oriented framework that links epidemiological state variables, contact structure, population immunity, mobility, interventions and uncertainty quantification to decision-relevant outputs. The novelty of this review lies in repositioning mpox modelling from retrospective explanation toward predictive readiness. A forecasting-first approach can strengthen early warning, targeted vaccination, communication planning and health-system preparedness, particularly in settings where surveillance is delayed, incomplete or geographically fragmented.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization: Current Status and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier for improving power grid stability and enhancing energy storage systems. Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) are electrochemical converters used to produce electricity from green hydrogen. Therefore, PEMFCs have been used in several industrial applications covering the transportation sector, aerospace applications, and distributed electrical energy generation. However, the multidisciplinary characteristics of PEMFCs make modelling and efficiency analysis a difficult task, resulting in limitations in the wider deployment of this new electricity generator. PEMFCs are characterized by strongly coupled transport, thermal, electrochemical, and degradation phenomena. High-performance computational machines have been used to investigate and analyze the degradation phenomena in PEMFCs. Despite this, this approach provides a detailed physical understanding of degradation levels, but the costly repeated simulation results in limitations in the utilization of this approach. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have been used to overcome such problems. Indeed, AI and ML have become powerful tools for the modelling and analysis of multidisciplinary systems due to their ability to predict results based on experimental results, sensor outputs, images and numerical simulations. In this context, this paper sheds light on the applications of AI, ML and digital twins in the field of modelling, design and degradation phenomena analysis of PEMFCs. The main phenomena taking place in PEMFCs, including reactant transport, gas–liquid flow, gas diffusion layer anisotropy, water management, heat transfer, transient behavior, and scale bridging and their effects on PEMFC performance degradation, are analyzed. Artificial neural networks, convolutional and recurrent architectures, Gaussian-process and ensemble methods, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), Bayesian optimization, metaheuristics, reinforcement learning, and hybrid digital-twin frameworks have different performances and they can be used for improving PEMFC modelling and phenomena analysis. Particular attention is given to the integration of physics-based and AI-driven models for PEMFC performance prediction, degradation assessment, optimization, and digital twin development. The review critically discusses existing applications, emerging approaches, and their limitations regarding experimental validation, uncertainty quantification, data availability, and generalization under varying operating conditions. Finally, future research directions are identified, emphasizing physics-informed modeling, degradation-aware digital twins, and reliable AI-assisted optimization and control.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a contribution to the development of evolutionary fuzzy optimization control for computational intelligence (CI)‐based robust visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) in autonomous mobile robots. The proposed SLAM method integrates visual perception, image processing, model predictive control (MPC), and fuzzy logic to improve localization robustness and map consistency. Some CI techniques are employed for image processing in the proposed ORB (Oriented fast and Rotated Brief)‐SLAM3 VSLAM framework. An interval Type‐2 fuzzy system is incorporated with MPC to develop the intelligent SLAM controller, called IT2FMPC for autonomous mobile robots. Moreover, an evolutionary genetic algorithm (GA) optimization strategy is employed to adaptively refine fuzzy membership functions and rule sets. The optimized GA‐IT2FMPC controller is integrated into the VSLAM to improve feature selection, motion estimation, and loop‐closure consistency. Numerical simulations and comparative studies conducted on publicly available datasets validate the performance and superiority of the developed VSLAM method. A physical experimental differential‐drive robot is constructed to demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces pose error and generates more consistent maps when compared with representative state‐of‐the‐art methods.

The control and experimental groups received different levels of instruction on Digital Electronics using Project Based Methods. The three dimensions considered when evaluating student learning were: (1) analog components; (2) active components; and (3) power supply systems using programming through the use of Arduino. A 20-item, true-false (dichotomous) instrument was developed, piloted, and validated by “expert opinion” as well as calculated using KMO (0.680) and internal consistency (KR-20 = 0.814). Pre-test results did not produce statistically significance between the two groups (p > 0.05), indicating the groups were statistical equivalent at the start of the research project. Posttest results indicated the experimental group experienced significant improvements compared to the control group in each of the three dimensions (p < 0.05). This study provides evidence that the utilization of low-cost embedded systems in combination with PBL methodology can promote improved understanding of conceptual material as well as greater development of practical skills. The findings from this study provide empirical support for the use of structured active learning methodologies in higher education environments that may have limited resources.

This study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of four advanced ensemble machine learning (ML) models, namely CatBoost, Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGBoost), LightGBM, and AdaBoost, for SOC estimation using a real-world dataset acquired from a BMW i3 EV equipped with a 60 Ah lithium-ion battery pack. Model hyperparameters were optimized using Optuna-based Bayesian optimization, while model generalization capability was assessed through cross-validation and holdout testing. Performance of the investigated ML models was evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), standard deviation of residuals (STD.DEV), maximum error (MAX), coefficient of determination ( \(R^2\) ), distribution-based error analysis, and noise sensitivity assessment. All investigated boosting models outperformed conventional benchmarks such as random forest and extreme learning machine. Among them, CatBoost achieved the highest prediction accuracy with an RMSE of 5.0386% and an MAE of 3.7333%, whereas AdaBoost demonstrated superior robustness with the lowest MAX error. Furthermore, Explainable Artificial Intelligence was incorporated using SHapley Additive exPlanations to quantify feature importance and enhance the transparency and interpretability of SOC prediction mechanisms.

papers.title: Maintaining reliable relationships between original conditions, representations, transformations, and outcomes
papers.abstract: This research formalizes a cross-domain source-fidelity framework within SICOHERENCE™ (Structural Intelligence Coherence), investigating the preservation of referential integrity, representational accuracy, transformation invariance, provenance continuity, and outcome consistency across interconnected information-processing systems. The proposed architecture distinguishes internal logical consistency from source-relative coherence by examining how distortions originate within representational encodings, propagate through hierarchical transformation and transmission pathways, and produce consequential deviations at the observable output layer. The framework integrates domain-specific distortion metrics, provenance-aware verification, structural invariant preservation, uncertainty quantification, and evidence-based correction protocols. Using the Sefirotic functional hierarchy, Hod corresponds to representation and classification, Yesod to integration and information transmission, and Malkuth to observable manifestation and operational consequences. Applications span human cognitive classification and identity attribution, artificial intelligence inference pipelines, automated decision architectures, and physical measurement systems. A comparative experimental methodology is proposed to evaluate upstream error detection, distortion propagation, corrective intervention efficacy, and measurable source-fidelity restoration. The central proposition is that structural coherence requires more than the absence of internal contradiction; it requires preservation of reliable, traceable relationships between original conditions, their representations, subsequent transformations, and manifested outcomes.

papers.title: Quasi-Steady Roll Plane Analysis and Metaheuristic Optimization for Enhancing Lateral Stability of Electric Vehicles using Active Height Control
papers.abstract: With the increasing adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs), the need for ensuring safe driving arises obviously. Though the EVs are designed to have a lower Center of Gravity (CG) height compared to Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles (ICEVs), due to their dynamic operating and road conditions, probabilities of rollover risk prevail. In order to ensure lateral stability and mitigate rollover risk, this paper presents the application of a metaheuristic optimization method to get the optimal key design parameters, one of which is the CG height, which is used as a reference signal to the Model Predictive Controller (MPC) of an Active Height Control (AHC) system comprising a hydraulic active suspension system at each of the wheels. The key parameters that influence the quasi-steady lateral acceleration are first optimized using the Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm (SFLA), and the results are benchmarked against the Genetic Algorithm (GA) to prove the salient feature of SFLA. A constrained Model Predictive Control (MPC) system that could estimate the disturbance and track the CG height offset-free is developed to modulate the vehicle’s CG height to the SFLA reference. The SFLA, GA and MPC are simulated using MATLAB coding. Simulation results of SFLA and GA are tabulated. The AHC system simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively maintains the CG height near its optimal value while minimizing lateral acceleration. Furthermore, the rollover index is also significantly reduced, remaining well below critical safety thresholds. An experimental demonstration comprising a LVDT with a metric micrometer to emulate measurement of CG height in real-time, associated signal conditioning circuit to derive a usable voltage and a servo positioning system to emulate electro-hydraulic valve functioning in the Hydraulic active suspension system is also presented to prove the feasibility of the proposed methods real-time implementation and control.

papers.title: A sliding annular in situ bioprinting strategy for rapid and robust fabrication of small-diameter vascular grafts.
papers.abstract: In situ bioprinting is an emerging technology with significant potential for organ repair, enabling the direct reconstruction of tissue at the injury site. This technique is particularly advantageous for urgent medical interventions. However, research on in situ printing of blood vessels remains limited. Here, we present a portable sliding annular in situ printing (SAIP) technique. Our system utilizes a ring-shaped printhead with multiple nozzles to directly deposit bioink onto a sacrificial scaffold bridging blood vessel ends. The bioink exhibits rapid crosslinking, robust mechanical properties, and strong adhesion, enabling the formation of a complete tubular structure after scaffold dissolution. This platform is designed for ease of use in emergency settings. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through successful carotid artery repair, highlighting its potential for clinical applications in in situ treatments.

papers.title: Functional Construction Strategies and Multidimensional Applications of Kidney Organoids.
papers.abstract: Kidney diseases represent a major global health burden, highlighting the need for advanced human-relevant models to investigate disease mechanisms and develop therapeutic strategies. Stem cell-derived kidney organoids have emerged as powerful human-relevant platforms that recapitulate key aspects of kidney development and enable the modeling of renal diseases. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in kidney organoid construction and characterization and highlights key bioengineering strategies for improving their structural and functional properties. These strategies include decellularized extracellular matrix scaffolds, 3D bioprinting, genetic engineering, vascularization, and organoid-on-a-chip technologies. Their broad biomedical applications in disease modeling, drug screening, toxicity assessment, and regenerative medicine are further discussed. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are addressed, with emphasis on improving reproducibility, maturation, and functional relevance to advance the translational potential of kidney organoids.

papers.title: A 3D-Printed Model of Human Lactation.
papers.abstract: Engineering physiologically relevant breast in vitro models remains challenging due to the gland's complex three-dimensional microanatomy, together with the need for epithelial polarity and hormone responsiveness. To overcome these challenges, fabrication methods are needed that rapidly create alveoli-scale structures with efficient diffusion and sustained hormonal stimulation. Here, Filamented Light (FLight) biofabrication is leveraged to print highly porous, ECM-based hydrogel scaffolds directly within standard Transwell inserts with separate apical and basal access. FLight's speckle-patterned laser generates multiscale scaffold architectures that integrate FLight channels (∼15 µm) to promote diffusion with alveoli-inspired cylindrical microwell arrays (Ø100, Ø150, and Ø200 µm) that impose geometric constraints to guide epithelial organization. Each insert is printed in <10 s and incorporates slow-release prolactin microcrystals to provide lactogenic stimulation in situ. Primary human milk-derived mammary epithelial cells (milk MECs) were seeded onto the constructs. There, milk MECs line the printed microwells, establish zona occludens-1-positive tight junctions, and express lactation-associated markers (prolactin receptor and β-casein), alongside milk fat globules and intracellular lipid droplets. Collectively, this rapidly reconfigurable FLight platform enables high-throughput generation of hormone-responsive human mammary microtissues for lactation-focused studies and is adaptable to other lumen-forming epithelia.
